text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes treatment options focus on lowering blood sugar levels and managing overall health through lifestyle habits, medications, and sometimes surgery.
snippet_highlighted_words: lifestyle habits, medications, and sometimes surgery

list.snippet: Healthy eating: Choose a balanced meal plan with lean proteins, complex carbohydrates, and non-starchy vegetables.
Regular exercise: Get at least 150 minutes of moderate physical activity, like walking or strength training, each week.
Weight loss: Aim to lose 5% or more of your body weight to help your body use insulin better.
Blood sugar tracking: Monitor your glucose levels regularly using a home meter or a continuous monitor.
Metformin: This is the most common first-line oral pill. It lowers sugar production in the liver and helps your muscles use insulin.
GLP-1 receptor agonists: These are injectable drugs (like semaglutide) that boost insulin, lower blood sugar, and help with weight loss.
SGLT2 inhibitors: These pills help your kidneys remove extra sugar through your urine while protecting your heart and kidneys.
Sulfonylureas: These older oral medications tell your pancreas to make more insulin.
DPP-4 inhibitors: These pills help keep blood sugar down without causing weight gain.
Thiazolidinediones (TZDs): These pills improve your body's sensitivity to insulin.
Insulin: If other drugs do not work well enough, you can inject synthetic insulin using a pen, syringe, or pump.
Weight-loss (bariatric) surgery: This procedure reduces stomach size and can significantly improve or remit type 2 diabetes in qualifying, severely overweight patients.

text_blocks.snippet: For more official guidance on managing your care, visit the American Diabetes Association or review the Mayo Clinic Diabetes Guide.
